newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich says Congress may miss July 4 budget deadline.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich says Congress may miss July 4 budget deadline.

text.p: Congress could take longer than expected to come up with tax and spending measures that conform to the balanced-budget agreement, House Speaker Newt Gingrich said Friday.
Up to now, Republican leaders on Capitol Hill have been saying they expected separate bills to be hammered out and sent to President Clinton for signing before the July 4 holiday.
But Gingrich told reporters in his home district that lawmakers were no longer likely to meet that deadline.
"We're going to do everything we can to get it done by the fourth of July. But it may run a little bit longer than that," the Georgia Republican said.
A measure that Gingrich described as a "spending" bill would curb Medicare spending and make cuts in other domestic programmes. Meanwhile, a separate tax bill would enact $85 billion in net tax cuts.
The speaker said the process was being held up by the sheer size of the undertaking.
